_comment: Counted-metrics ledger, family 'ram_per_peer' (#2137). The WIDE rows bench/ram_census_pins.json already pins (bench_conn_ram, #2134) are NOT pinned here: they read their value from that file and are gated in the mode its activation block declares, with its band. The WIDE rows that file does not pin (remote subscriptions, the buffer a peer keeps after a 16 KiB frame, #2171) are measured rows, read from the bench_conn_ram transcript and pinned here. MID rows are static counts.
title: RAM per peer

rows.moved_by: #2272 (lock-free server broadcast, #2263: the session's 8 B next link puts it one block class up, 290 -> 306 B; re-pinned by #2512)
rows.waiver: #2144 maintainer ruling (one ring per (peer, vertex), review blocker 4): the 24 B egress slot is the at-rest cost of the shared-frame egress; rings are drawn only while frames wait. Since #2176 removed the WS session's stream buffer, the same slot shows on the ws-server row too (+32 B, one block class). The +16 B of #2272 is the price of a broadcast that holds no lock across its writes (#2263, recorded in core/CHANGELOG.md): each session carries the 8 B link of the chain the walk follows.
rows.note: Goal: today's value less the per-peer transport_t stand-in (120 B on x86), deleted by the #2136 peer record.

rows.moved_by: #2144 (one shared-frame egress, one ring per (peer, vertex))
rows.basis: sizeof(tr::net::egress_peer_t) on x86-64, pinned by its static_assert (16 B on a 32-bit target): the lane round, the frame on the wire and its offset, the strike count, the role and the writability flag. A ring is drawn per (peer, vertex) only while frames wait, so an idle peer holds this slot and nothing else.

rows.moved_by: #2326 (per-peer lane lock, #2310: egress_t loses its 40 B std::mutex, link base 600 -> 568 B; on ws-server after #2272's 8 B first_ head had moved it 600 -> 616 B; #2351's 8 B tail-padding loss taken back by #2512)
rows.waiver: #2198 maintainer ruling 2026-10-16 (frozen peers are closed by an app-driven check, implemented per transport vertex): +16 B per server link object, not per peer. It is two 8 B members of stream_endpoint_t, which every stream link inherits: frozen_closed_ (std::atomic<std::size_t>, the count of peers the check closed, read by frozen_closed()) and live_since_ (std::uint64_t, the app-supplied `now` at which the check last saw this endpoint make progress; only the dialer's one-peer record reads it, a server judges each session by its own 8 B live_since). tx_moved_ sits in an existing padding hole and costs 0 B.
rows.note: Per link, not per peer: what an idle server link holds before any peer. #2136 sets no number; it holds.

rows.note: Goal: no receive segment at rest (#2142 met it, 1,768 -> 216 B); 232 B is what the pool arm reads.

rows.moved_by: #2548 (re-measured; the 288 B seed was never read from an image)
rows.basis: sizeof(httpd_ws_link_t::session_t) on riscv32, read as DW_AT_byte_size of session_t in httpd_ws_link.cpp.obj of the esp32c6 full_node build (espressif/idf:release-v6.0) at 408c6e4e2: subject[128] + endpoint_str[52] + name[25] (205 B of strings), link_counters_t (24 B), ws_assembler_t (20 B, #2483), the TX frame + wait queue (48 B, #2195), live_since (8 B, #2198). The TX queue peak (#2464) adds 0 B: link_counters_t::tx_queue_peak fills that block's padding before connected_at_us (24 B, 48 B with traffic stats, either way), and the slot's one-byte tx_peak the padding after tx_spare_used. Goal from #2136 user story 27.
rows.waiver: Bookkeeping waiver granted by the maintainer (ruling 37, 2026-11-06): none of this growth had been waived when it shipped. The same method at the seed commit f6007ae39 (#2137) reads 336 B, so the 288 B seed was 48 B short from the start. Since the seed, +40 B: +20 B #2196/#2197 (#2195: tx_frame_t gains the 4 B lane word, tx_wire gives way to tx_head/tx_tail/tx_spare/tx_spare_used); +12 B #2207 (#2198: live_since 8 B plus 4 B of alignment; tx_moved and tx_frozen sit in padding); +4 B #2233 (kSlotNameChars 22 -> 24, name 23 -> 25 B, plus alignment); +4 B #2502 (#2483: ws_assembler_t 20 B replaces the 16 B asm_buf).

rows.basis: One recv task per esp_ws_client / posix client link at the pthread default stack (CONFIG_PTHREAD_TASK_STACK_SIZE_DEFAULT in full_node). Goal from #2136 user story 1.
Worker task + the socket's recv task, 12288 B each. Goal: the wait module (#2136) leaves no per-connection task.

_toolchain: Byte counts follow sizeof, so a run on another toolchain is reported in warn mode and never turns CI red.
